einzeiler: Celebrating 15 years of the screenwriting podcast with a look back at its origins.
kurzfassung: The hosts celebrate the 15th anniversary of their screenwriting podcast by reflecting on its humble beginnings in 2011. They listen to a newly discovered pre-show recording and discuss how the media landscape has evolved over the past decade and a half. Additionally, they answer listener questions regarding pitching assignments, depicting the passage of time, and the lengthy production schedules of modern television.
stichpunkte: Celebrating 15 years of recording the podcast weekly without interruption
Uncovering and playing an audio recording from June 2011 before the show even had a name
Comparing the movie and television landscape of 2011 with the current entertainment industry
Answering the very first listener question ever submitted about pitching takes on rewrite assignments
Discussing cinematic and visual techniques for showing the passage of time without title cards
Explaining why modern television production schedules are significantly longer than network TV in the past

kapitel.titel: Reflecting on Episode One and Changes
Showing the Passage of Time in Scripts
Why Making TV Shows Takes So Long

clips.hook: Unearthing a 2011 recording featuring a noisy pug
clips.text: The hosts recall that background clicking noises on their earliest audio files were caused by a furry pet walking around during the recording.

clips.hook: Selling a positive vision during a rewrite meeting
clips.text: Writers are advised to focus on pitching an enthusiastic, forward-looking take rather than spending the meeting tearing down the existing script.

clips.hook: Using growing props and background elements to show time
clips.text: Planting a tree that grows taller or tracking a neighbor's baby growing into a teenager can effectively indicate the passage of time visually.

clips.hook: The relentless grind of producing high-end television
clips.text: Showrunners often transition immediately from finishing post-production on one season straight into working on the next with barely any break.

clips.hook: Losing high school creative writing to old technology
clips.text: Early writing done on vintage computers from decades ago is often permanently lost because the original floppy disks and files can no longer be opened.

beschreibung:
The year was 2011. We had Occupy Wall Street, Hangover II, 50 Shades of Grey… and a podcast named Scriptnotes. On this episode, John and Craig celebrate their podcast Quinceañera, marking fifteen years together on mic.
They reflect on their very first episode, the content and cultural moments that marked 2011, and everything that's changed since.
In our bonus segment for premium subscribers, John and Craig look forward fifteen years to make predictions on the year 2041.
